[[List of Lowe's Senior CLASS Award men's basketball winners|2010 Lowe's Senior CLASS Award]] }} '''Da'Sean Butler''' (born January 25, 1988 in {{city-state|Newark|New Jersey}}) is a [[college basketball]] [[Forward (basketball)|forward]] for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. ==Collegiate career== ===Freshman season=== Desean Butler scored a career high 21 points in a game against Seton Hall. Against [[Slippery Rock University of Pennsylvania|Slippery Rock]], Butler had 15 points and nine rebounds off the bench, then had eight points against [[University of Arkansas|Arkansas]]. He had 9 points against [[North Carolina State]], then 10 points and six rebounds against [[Duquesne University|Duquesne]]. Butler scored 14 points against [[The Citadel (military college)|The Citadel]], 16 points against [[UConn]], 7 points against [[Villanova University|Villanova]], and then six points against [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]]. He then scored 9 points and a season-high 10 rebounds against [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]], followed by 12 points and six rebounds against [[University of South Florida|South Florida]]. Butler then had 14 points and 8 rebounds against [[University of Cincinnati|Cincinnati]], 17 points against [[Rutgers]], and a team-high 14 points against [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]] in the [[Backyard Brawl]]. In the huge upset win over [[UCLA]], Butler had 13 points, while scoring 17 points against [[University of Louisville|Louisville]] in the [[Big East]] Tournament. The Mountaineers eventually made it in the [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT]] Tournament, and all the way to the finals. In the finals win against [[Clemson University|Clemson]], Butler had 20 points, as the Mountaineers were named NIT Champions. Butler was named to the [[Big East|all-Big East]] freshman team, while leading the Mountaineers to an [[National Invitation Tournament|NIT Championship]]. Butler averaged 10.1 points per game, averaging 23.3 minutes per game off the bench, while also averaging 3.5 rebounds per game. ===Sophomore season=== After the [[National Invitation Tournament|2007 NIT Championship]] win, head coach [[John Beilein]] announced he would be leaving [[West Virginia University]] to take the head coaching position at the [[University of Michigan]]. Soon after, former head coach of [[Kansas State|Kansas State's]] basketball team and former West Virginia alumnus, [[Bob Huggins]] announced he accepted an offer to coach at [[West Virginia University|West Virginia]]. In the season-opening exhibition game against [[Mountain State University|Mountain State]], Butler earned his first career start as the Mountaineers won 88–65. Butler scored 16 points and added 8 rebounds and three assists as he and fellow-guard [[Darris Nichols]] both went into double-digits in points. In the season-opener against [[University of Arkansas at Monticello|Arkansas-Monticello]], Butler scored 14 points while also grabbing a season-high 9 rebounds. In the 72–74 loss to [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]], Butler happened to score 16 points and grab 7 rebounds, while he scored 13 in the victories over [[New Mexico State]] and [[Auburn University|Auburn]]. Butler scored a season-high 18 points against [[Duquesne University|Duquesne]], while also grabbing 8 rebounds. He then scored 14 points against Maryland County, grabbing 9 rebounds, and [[Radford University]], and then scored 10 against [[Canisius College|Canisius]]. In the 88–82 loss to [[University of Oklahoma|Oklahoma]], Butler scored 15 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the loss to [[University of Notre Dame|Notre Dame]], Butler only scored 8 points but did grab 5 rebounds. Then in the victory over [[Marquette University|Marquette]], Butler scored 13 points with 5 rebounds, but in the loss to [[University of Louisville|Louisville]] he only scored 8 again. In the victory over [[University of Syracuse|Syracuse]], Butler grabbed 6 rebounds to go along with his 13 points. Butler was key in the [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]] victory with 19 points and 9 rebounds. Butler recorded his first double-double of the season in the loss to [[University of South Florida|USF]], with 15 points and 12 rebounds. In the 66–64 victory over [[Marshall University|Marshall]], Butler scored 18 points – including the game-winning shot in the lane with 6 seconds left. Then in the 58–57 loss to #9 [[Georgetown University|Georgetown]], Butler attempted to score the game-winning points again. However, his layup attempt was blocked by [[Patrick Ewing, Jr.]]. The call was questionable however, as many believe it was actually a [[goaltending]] which would result in the points being rewarded and the Mountaineer-victory.{{cite web|author=7:00 PM ET, January 26, 2008WVU Coliseum, Morgantown, WV |url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280260277 |title=ESPN – Georgetown vs. West Virginia – Recap – January 26, 2008 |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=January 26, 2008 |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} However, Butler finished with 12 points and 4 rebounds. In an 81–63 victory over [[Rutgers]], Butler scored 12 points. He then followed that game with 15 points and 8 rebounds against [[Seton Hall]]. In the 78–56 loss to [[Villanova University|Villanova]], Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 7 rebounds. In the 80–53 victory over [[Providence College|Providence]], Butler scored 13 points and grabbed 4 rebounds. In the 85–73 victory over [[DePaul]] to gain the 20th win of the season, Butler scored 14 points and grabbed 13 rebounds for his second double-double of the season. In the 79–71 loss to [[UConn|Connecticut]], Butler scored 9 points and added 7 rebounds. In the home finale victory over the [[Pittsburgh Panthers]], 76–62, Butler scored 10 points and grabbed 6 rebounds. In the regular season finale, a 83–74 overtime victory over Providence, Butler scored 18 points, grabbed 10 rebounds, and dished 5 assists to finish the regular season. He finished the season with 12.5 points and 6.1 rebounds per game. In the 58–53 victory over Providence to open the [[Big East]] Tournament, Butler scored 17 points and added 9 rebounds. In the second round of the tourney, the Mountaineers upset the #15-ranked [[Connecticut Huskies]], 78–72. Butler contributed with 17 points and a team-high 9 rebounds. However, as the Mountaineers lost 55–72 in the semifinal matchup against the #8 [[Georgetown Hoyas]], Butler scored 16 points with 3 rebounds and assists. In the first round of the [[2008 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], Butler scored 19 points with 7 rebounds as the #7-seed Mountaineers defeated the #10-seed [[Arizona Wildcats]]. In the second round, the Mountaineers upset the #2-seed [[Duke Blue Devils]] 73–67, with Butler scoring 8 points and grabbing 5 rebounds. Then, in the Sweet 16 loss in overtime to #3-seed [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]], Butler scored 16 points and grabbed 7 rebounds. Butler finished his sophomore season by averaging 12.9 points and 6.2 rebounds per game. During the Mountaineers Sweet 16 NCAA Tournament run, Butler averaged 14.3 points and 6.3 rebounds per game. ===Junior season=== Butler began his junior season under returning head coach [[Bob Huggins]] in the 98–78 exhibition win over [[Mountain State University|Mountain State]]. In the victory, Butler led the Mountaineers with 38 points and 11 rebounds. In the regular season opener against [[Elon University|Elon]], Butler scored 19 points and totaled 6 rebounds and steals. Against [[Longwood University|Longwood]], he then totaled 12 points and 4 rebounds. Opening the Las Vegas Invitational Tournament, the Mountaineers defeated [[Delaware State]], with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 7 rebounds. He then scored 12 against [[Iowa Hawkeyes|Iowa]], and before scoring 7 points with 9 boards in the loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats|Kentucky]]. However, the Mountaineers then defeated [[Ole Miss|Mississippi]], with Butler scoring 22 points and grabbing 10 rebounds – his first double-double of the season. As the Mountaineers then beat [[Cleveland State]], Butler led the team with 18 points. In the 68–65 last-second loss to #22 [[Davidson University|Davidson]] and [[Stephen Curry (basketball)|Stephen Curry]] in [[Madison Square Garden]], Butler led the Mountaineers with 24 points and 14 rebounds – his second double-double in three games. Butler reached his 1,000 career points during the Miami University victory, in which he scored a career-high 28 points out of the team's 82–46 victory and also had 5 rebounds. Butler then had 11 points against [[Radford University|Radford]], followed by 16 points and 6 rebounds in the 76–48 victory over #13 [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Ohio State]]. In the 92–66 win over [[Seton Hall]], Butler had 18 points, 9 rebounds and 5 assists. In the next loss to #5 [[Connecticut Huskies|UConn]], 61–55, Butler scored 13 points and had 5 steals. As the Mountaineers then lost to #15 [[Marquette Golden Eagles|Marquette]], Butler scored 16 points and had 5 rebounds. Butler then had 17 points and 7 rebounds in the victory over [[Marshall University|Marshall]]. Against [[South Florida Bulls|South Florida]], Butler scored 27 points with 4 rebounds, and then he totaled 27 points and 8 rebounds in the win over #14 [[Georgetown Hoyas|Georgetown]]. In the following loss to #4 [[Pittsburgh Panthers|Pittsburgh]], Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the win over [[St. John's University (New York)|St. John's]], Butler scored 21 points and had 7 rebounds. Butler recorded his fifth-consecutive 20-point game with 23 points against #7 [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]] to go with 8 rebounds. Butler followed the Louisville loss with 23 points, 4 rebounds, 4 assists, and 4 steals against [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]]. Butler's consecutive 20-point game streak ended at six games against [[Providence University|Providence]] with his 17 points and 9 rebounds in the 86–59 victory. In the [[Backyard Brawl]] loss to #4 [[Pittsburgh Panthers|Pittsburgh]], Butler only scored 4 points in limited playing time due to foul trouble. On February 13, the Mountaineers defeated #13 [[Villanova University|Villanova]] 93–72. In the victory, Butler scored a career-high 43 points; 24 points coming in the first-half. Butler's point total was the second-highest individual scoring performance in a [[Big East]] conference game since the 2002–03 season, only one-point shy of [[Marcus Hatten|Marcus Hatten's]] 44 point performance in 2003.{{cite web|author=9:00 PM ET, February 13, 2009WVU Coliseum, Morgantown, WV |url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290440277 |title=Villanova Wildcats vs. West Virginia Mountaineers – Recap – February 13, 2009 – ESPN |publisher=Scores.espn.go.com |date=February 13, 2009 |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} His 43 points were the third-most ever scored in the [[WVU Coliseum]], the most by a WVU player in conference play ever and the first 40-point performance since Lowes Moore in 1978.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=14176&cat=exclusives |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date= |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} In the following 79–68 win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]], Butler had 19 points, 4 rebounds and 4 assists. He followed with 12 points and 4 assists in the win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]]. In the 65–61 loss to [[Cincinnati Bearcats|Cincinnati]], Butler had 8 points and 4 assists. He then had 9 points and 12 rebounds in a win over [[South Florida Bulls|USF]]. Butler then had a double-double in the win over [[DePaul]] with 16 points and 10 rebounds. In the regular season finale against #6 [[Louisville Cardinals|Louisville]], Butler scored 10 points with 10 rebounds for a second-straight double-double. Following the 62–59 loss, he was named to the All-[[Big East]] second team.{{cite web|url=http://westvirginia.scout.com/2/845459.html |title=Scout.com: Three Mountaineers Earn Big East Awards |publisher=Westvirginia.scout.com |date=March 8, 2009 |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} In the second round of the Big East Tournament against Notre Dame, Butler scored 20 points and grabbed 5 rebounds. In the quarterfinals' 74–60 win over #2 [[Pittsburgh Panthers]], Butler scored 16 points with 4 assists and 3 rebounds despite sitting out due to 4 personal fouls. In the semifinal round, a 74–69 loss to #20 [[Syracuse Orangemen|Syracuse]], Butler scored 21 points and had 6 rebounds. In the Big East Tournament, Butler averaged 19 points and 4.6 rebounds. However, the Mountaineers were upset in the first round of the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] by [[University of Dayton|Dayton]], 68–60, with Butler scoring 12 points and grabbing 5 rebounds. Butler finished his junior season with an average of 17.1 points per game and 5.9 rebounds per game. Butler had a season-high 43 points against Villanova and a season-high 14 rebounds against Davidson. Butler scored 20 or more points 12 times in the campaign.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=14405&cat=exclusives |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date=March 20, 2009 |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} ===Senior season=== Butler was invited to the 2009 USA Basketball Men's World University Games Team training camp prior to his senior season.{{cite web|url=http://www.msnsportsnet.com/page.cfm?story=14687&cat=exclusives |title=West Virginia University Mountaineers |publisher=MSNsportsNET.Com |date= |accessdate=March 29, 2010}} Butler and the Top10-ranked Mountaineers opened up the season with a win over Loyola-Maryland, in which Butler recorded 26 points and 7 rebounds. In a later win over Portland, Butler scored 26 points with 6 rebounds. At the end of December, Butler hit a game-winning jumper to defeat Marquette, adding to his 17 total points. After losing three games in early to mid-January, Butler and the Mountaineers bounced back with a win over #25 Ohio State and then a win over Louisville in which Butler scored 27 points. In a following win over St. John's, Butler scored 33 points, then he added 32 points in a triple overtime loss to #23 Pittsburgh. The Mountaineers ended their regular season with a 68–66 victory over #6 Villanova in which Butler had a double-double: 21 points and 10 rebounds. In the Mountaineers' opening game of the Big East Tournament, West Virginia defeated Cincinnati with help from Butler, who banked in the game-winning three-pointer with no time left to win 54–51. In the following 53–51 victory over Notre Dame in the semifinals, Butler scored 24 points. In the championship game, Butler again led the Mountaineers to victory with the game-winning bucket over #22 Georgetown. The victory was the first ever Big East title for the Mountaineers. Entering the NCAA Tournament as a two-seed, the Mountaineers handled Morgan State in the opening round. Butler scored 28 points and added 8 rebounds in the second round victory over Missouri. After defeating Washington in the Sweet 16, the Mountaineers upset the 1-seed and tourney favorite Kentucky Wildcats 73–66, to advance to the school's second Final Four appearance. Butler had 18 points in the Elite Eight victory, including finishing 4–8 from the 3-point line. Butler and Duke's [[Jon Scheyer]] were the only finalists in 2010's [[Final Four]] for the [[Lowe's Senior CLASS Award|Lowe's Senior CLASS Award for Men's Basketball]],{{cite web|url=http://www.wbir.com/sports/college/basketball/story.aspx?storyid=117625&catid=159 |title=Knoxville, TN | Wall, Scheyer, Turner chosen to Wooden All-American team |publisher=WBIR.com |date=January 4, 2010 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} which on April 3, 2010, was awarded to Butler. Later that day, in the second half of the Final Four loss to the [[2009–10 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke Blue Devils]], Butler injured his left knee. Early reports are that Butler tore his ACL, sprained his MCL and sustained two bone bruises. He was driving hard to the basket and the knee appeared to give way as he planted on it, while Coach Huggins initially seemed convinced Butler was fouled on the play- that does not seem to be the cause of the injury. Butler is one of 10 finalists for the 2010 [[John R. Wooden Award]].{{cite web|url=http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/news/story?id=5048730 |title=Duke's Jon Scheyer, West Virginia's Da'Sean Butler among Wooden Award finalists – ESPN |publisher=Sports.espn.go.com |date=January 1, 2008 |accessdate=April 2, 2010}} It is given to the National Player of the Year in college basketball by The [[Los Angeles Athletic Club]].{{cite web|url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4200&ATCLID=204865052 |title="Scheyer and Singler Among Candidates for Wooden Award", goduke.com, January 5, 2010, accessed February 8, 2010 |publisher=Goduke.com |date=January 5, 2010 |accessdate=March 15, 2010}} ==External links== * [http://wvustats.com/mbasketball/player.php?team_id=308&person_id=51942 WVU Profile] ==See also== * [[2010 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} {{Lowe's Senior CLASS Award - Basketball}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Butler, Da'sean}} [[Category:1988 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from New Jersey]] [[Category:West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball players]] [[Category:People from Newark, New Jersey]]
